description: Generate a GUI component following metadata-driven element prefix conventions. Enforces naming rules, conflict detection, and validation at creation time.
context: Use when writing any interactive UI element (button, input, toggle, modal, card, table, etc.) in this project
checklist: 1. DETERMINE ELEMENT TYPE: Identify which UI element type you are creating (button, input, toggle, modal, card, table, notification, etc.). Refer to .ai/coding-prefixes.md for complete registry.
2. GENERATE ELEMENT ID: Use the central controller (validation/gui_element_id.py) to generate a compliant ID. Command: `python validation/gui_element_id.py --type <TYPE> --name <NAME> --verbose`
3. CHECK FOR CONFLICTS: Before writing the component, verify the ID is unique. Command: `python validation/gui_element_id.py --find-conflicts --name <NAME>`
4. WRITE COMPONENT: Generate the UI component with the generated ID as the `id` attribute. Use the 2-letter prefix in the ID (e.g., `bu_submit_form` for buttons, `in_email_address` for inputs).
5. FOLLOW NAMING NORMALIZATION: The generator automatically converts camelCase/PascalCase to snake_case. Example: 'submitUserForm' → 'bu_submit_user_form'
6. APPLY TO ALL INTERACTIVE ELEMENTS: Add prefixed IDs to: buttons, toggles, inputs, checkboxes, selects, modals, cards, tables, tabs, notifications, badges, and any element that might be tested.
7. SCAN AND VALIDATE: After writing, run discovery to update the registry. Command: `python validation/discovery.py --scan-root ./src --output prefixes-found.json`
8. RUN EXISTENCE CHECKS: Verify your new element is discoverable. Command: `python validation/test_facility.py --registry prefixes-found.json`
9. REPORT SUCCESS: Confirm element ID generated, conflicts checked, component written, and validation passed
